item.description: Victor Wembanyama makes history by being the first player in 50 years with these numbers originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . In a 14-game slate on Wednesday, there were plenty of top-tier performances. Luka Doncic was once again brilliant for the Los Angeles Lakers with a 40-point night, and the same could be said about Denver Nuggets star Nikola Jokic with another triple-double to his name. Despite those amazing performances, they all pale in comparison when compared to San Antonio Spurs superstar Victor Wembanyama. The Frenchman had the night's best performance, posting a stat line of 52 points, 24 rebounds, and eight blocks to beat the Dallas Mavericks in a close game. Victor Wembanyama puts up historic numbers against the Mavericks For almost the entire game, the Spurs were in control against the Mavericks on Wednesday. That was why people were raving about Wembanyama in the first half, as he already had 29 points, 15 rebounds, and five blocks at halftime. However, the Mavericks staged a comeback in the second half. They almost won the game with a Kyrie Irving game-winner, but the Spurs defended it well, which led to a victory that complemented Wembanyama's performance. MORE: Victor Wembanyama goes viral for three blocks in 13 seconds It was a magical night for the French giant, and it seems that his teammates agree with that. Everyone knows he is the Spurs' superstar, so if he performs well, the atmosphere within the Spurs organization is much better. "When he gets in the vicinity of the paint, he’s just unstoppable to guard. So I mean we just gotta keep on finding ways to get him down there and then let him operate," Spurs guard Dylan Harper said about Wembanyama's impressive performance . Wembanyama is playing at an MVP level once again, as the Spurs have won their sixth straight game. After their slow start to the season, the Spurs fans were worried, but now, it seems that the Spurs have everyone else worried. A lot has happened since then. One thing that hasn’t happened, however, is a Premier League victory. Just one point from a possible 15 has been taken since we kicked off our continental adventure on home soil. Unfortunately, it has the potential to take the shine off our performance so far in the Europa League, and until we improve, any European game will be placed into the context of the two league games either side of it. item.title: Seven Changes for Sunderland For Tonight’s Game Against Zagreb?
item.description: SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 04: Regis Le Bris, Manager of Sunderland, speaks with his staff including First Team Coach Jose Fonte during the training session on MD-1 ahead of the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD4, at The Academy of Light on November 04, 2026 in Sunderland, England. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) | Getty Images What lessons have been learned from Saturday? What have the honest and frank conversations produced? We’ll find out in a matter of hours as the lads are back in action against Zagreb. Hopefully, we’ll see a huge change in attitude and application, as well as our intent and team cohesion, which has been sorely lacking in recent weeks. Le Bris has been given a stay of execution – will he take advantage of it? We’ll soon find out. Goalkeeper: Robin Roefs Roefs can’t be happy at present playing in front of a team that’s continually leaving him exposed – he’s produced some great saves in recent European games and hopefully he has a good night tonight. Defence: Thomas Meunier, Kevin Danso, Luke O’Nien, Dayann Methalie Trai Hume has played a lot of football recently and with an international break looming that’ll continue. Meunier needs a game so should hopefully start at right back, while Methalie will start on the left. A good show from him tonight could see him line up against Chelsea. In the centre, we’re likely to see Danso return – Mukiele is still out – while O’Nien could play alongside him. The other option is Alderete, but he’s completely out of sorts and needs to be taken out for a while. Midfield: Nilson Angulo, Granit Xhaka, Jules Ahoka, Chemsdine Talbi, Malick Fofana Talbi’s inclusion in the squad is a boost and he will surely come into the team – I’d like to see him play in the 10 as he looked good there against Brentford. I think this is a game Xhaka ideally would sit out, but his form and the troubles the team’s having means he probably should play; hopefully alongside Ahoka, who can provide legs and energy around him. On the wings, we need to go with two proper wingers, so hopefully Fofana will produce a good display on the left, and Angulo can carry on his good work against Poznan on the right. Striker: Wilson Isidor We don’t need to risk Brobbey, so Isidor should get an hour after 30 minutes at Coventry – he’s more than capable of causing teams problems, as long as the set up behind his is decent.

item.title: New CBA proposal adjusts salary cap, floor
item.description: ATLANTA, GA - MAY 13: A locked padlock and chain against two official MLB baseballs representing a potential lockout between Major League Baseball (MLB) and the Major League Baseball Players Association (MLBPA) for the 2027 MLB season, as photographed on May 13, 2026 in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by David J. Griffin/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Major League Baseball has amended its salary cap and floor proposal to the MLB Players Association. Now that the 2026 season is complete and baseball is into its offseason, MLB has proposed delaying the start of the salary cap and floor to the 2028 season. The rest of their proposals would begin with the 2027 season but the teams would have a full season to make adjustments to prepare themselves for the coming changes. The owners further proposed increasing the cap to $258.2 million from the original $245.3 million and the floor to $180.2 million from $171.2 million. The new numbers reflect a 50-50 split of the projected revenue for the 2028 season. A change to the retirement proposal The offer also includes $282 million in luxury tax revenue to be given to players in cash payments instead of being placed into retirement benefits. In the present system, when a team pays luxury tax, half of the money goes into player benefits and the other half to the teams. For the 2027 season, the league is offering to pay the retirement portion directly to the players. According to league estimates , $285,000 would go to each player who received a full year of service time, $213,400 to a player with three-quarters of a year of service, $142,300 to a player with a half year of service, and $71,100 to any player with a quarter year of service. Teams outside the guidelines Per the MLB numbers, 12 teams would have to raise payroll to meet the minimum proposed floor while eight teams would have to decrease their payroll to meet the cap. Those numbers are based on current payrolls and would change based on what teams spend in 2027. Players response The MLB Players Association predictably responded negatively to the new offer. “MLB owners continue to propose blowing up the current system and replacing it with one designed to line their pockets and increase their franchise values.” The statement continued, “a massive reduction in player compensation, elimination of fundamental player rights, plus a gutting of domestic and international amateur entry systems.” A statement virtually identical to the previous proposal from the owners. Sweetening the pot? This appears to be an attempt by the league to sweeten the deal for the players but doesn’t seem to have the desired effect. The baseline for the union is their unwillingness to accept a salary cap and floor as the start of negotiations. The current contract expires and 11:59 pm eastern time on Dec. 1. The owners have made it clear they intend to lock the players out if no deal is reached by that time.

How would you reflect on that campaign and what were the expectations among supporters heading into this season? Last season’s campaign went about as well as Dinamo wanted after not winning anything the season prior; they dominated and returned to their usual form. They always want to win the domestic double; they essentially take it for granted. So the real challenges/expectations come in Europe, with them being back in the UCL qualifiers; the club and the fans want to return to the UCL. This didn’t happen, as they lost to the Norwegian side, Viking, because of their poor defensive lapses in concentration, as they conceded two goals in quick succession in both legs. This left the fans mad at the higher-ups for not bringing in immediate improvements for the squad beforehand, and at the coach for the poor reactions from the team. Dinamo currently sit second behind Hajduk in the league and Saturday’s shock 1-0 defeat to Rudeš ultimately proved to be Mario Kovačević’s final match. What has gone wrong in recent weeks? It’s just the players’ form; everybody except Dion Drena Beljo is struggling to play at a good level game after game. The defence, especially, has been the most inconsistent. After claiming the title in 1936, the lads finished the 36/37 season in eighth place – 13 points behind winners Manchester City – and finished in the same position the following season, albeit just eight points shy of champions Arsenal. The FA Cup had once again been in tantalising grasp – only for Huddersfield Town to snatch the potential of the holders retaining the trophy with a semi-final defeat. 1938/39 began with a renewed determination to reclaim the title – or at least seriously compete for it – but on this day in 1938, Sunderland finally won their first home game of the season on their sixth attempt – climbing to 6th position in the top flight in the process. Unbeknown to anyone watching on that day, it would be the highest we’d rank in the table for eight years – and it signalled the end of an era for this talented Sunderland team. The 38/39 season saw us finish 16th, only six points off a relegation spot, after a run of just 5 wins in the season’s remaining 22 games saw us drift down the table, and the following season was curtailed due to the outbreak of WW2. item.title: An Introduction to Dinamo Zagreb: What Can Sunderland Expect?
item.description: On the occasion of the International tie Day at Saint Mark's square in front of Saint Mark church on upper town, Honour Cravat Regiment changing the guard on 18 Oct 2014, Zagreb,Croatia. (Photo by Alen Gurovic/NurPhoto) (Photo by NurPhoto/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Tonight, Sunderland play their second Europa League home game of the campaign, as the Lads welcome Dinamo Zagreb to Wearside. Here’s what you need to know about the Croatian champions! Zagreb: Croatia’s Capital With a population of around 750,000, Zagreb is Croatia’s largest city, and the use of its name dates back nearly 1000 years to 1094 AD. The city emerged from two medieval settlements (Gric and Kaptol) and began rapid development and expansion when the two combined in the 19th century. It has played a crucial role in the political history of Croatia, and in 1941 it became the capital of a Croatian puppet state controlled by the Axis powers. After being freed in 1945, Croatia became a part of Yugoslavia from the end of the Second World War until 1991. Zagreb was the centre of a newly independent Croatia during and following the Croatian War of Independence (1991-1995). On a lighter note, Zagreb is home to the world’s shortest public transport funicular, which connects the city’s old town to its newer Novi Zagreb area. It spans a total of 66m, and between its opening in 1890 to 1934, it was powered by steam. Nowadays, the journey is electrified and lasts approximately a minute. The city also keeps many of its old traditions. Every day at noon, a cannon is fired from Lotrščak Tower beside the funicular to mark midday. This has happened every day since 1877. Zagreb also has over 200 gas street lamps which are still lit manually every night, and this tradition dates back to 1863. There are also a number of weird and wonderful museums to visit in the Croatian capital. These include the Museum of Hangovers, the Museum of Laughter, the Museum of Broken Relationships, and a mushroom museum. Dinamo Zagreb: A Brief History Dinamo Zagreb were initially formed in 1911 when Croatia was a part of the Austro-Hungarian Empire. Upon the end of the Second World War, the club was dissolved by communist authorities; however, it was re-established just three days later on the ninth of June, 1945. The new club inherited the colours, nickname, badge and fanbase of the original club. Its name was changed to Croatia Zagreb in 1993 – a move which was seen as a political move to move away from the club’s communist past amidst Croatian independence. However, this name was never accepted by supporters, and the name Dinamo Zagreb was reinstated in the year 2000. Dinamo Zagreb is Croatia’s most successful club and has lifted the Croatian league 25 times, most recently last season, in which they finished 20 points ahead of second-placed Hajduk Split. item.description: SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 28: Regis Le Bris, head coach of Sunderland reacts on the sidelines during the Carabao Cup Fourth Round match between Sunderland and Brentford at Stadium of Light on October 28, 2026 in Sunderland, England. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’ve all seen how things have gone wrong over the last few days, weeks and months and a lot of errors could be attributed to Régis Le Bris over that period. It looks like the club are backing Le Bris for at least a little bit longer in the hope that he can figure the whole mess out and get some points on the board. Whether you agree with the decision or not, I’m sure many of you have some opinions on how he should go about changing our fortunes, and I’m no different! So, I thought it would be fun to have a look at some things he may consider to flip the script for the Lads in the coming weeks with the fair caveat that although I think these are fair points to raise, I believe that Le Bris is a truly gifted manager with more knowledge and experience of the game than I could ever hope to possess. For that reason, I’ll be offering some counters to each point for a bit of balance. Pick a style First up for me is to pick a style and to stick to it. item.description: Photo by Raj Mehta/Getty Images Calvin Johnson believes the Detroit Lions have had the talent to win a Super Bowl but insists they cannot reach the NFL’s biggest prize without being willing to spend big. The former wide receiver pointed to Matthew Stafford’s departure as an example of why Detroit needed to be more aggressive in building a championship-winning roster. Johnson spent his entire NFL career with the Lions before retiring at just 30 years old, but his relationship with the organisation has improved considerably in recent years. Calvin Johnson says Detroit Lions cannot win Super Bowl on a budget Speaking on the Chasing No. 1 podcast, Johnson explained why he believed Detroit had the necessary pieces during his time with the franchise. “The biggest thing for me is that, I used to always say, we tell everybody we got the team here in Detroit. We had the dudes, but you can’t win a Super Bowl on a budget, man. You got to go all in.” Johnson also pointed to teams making significant moves to add the final pieces needed to compete for a championship. He then brought up Stafford, who won the Super Bowl with the Los Angeles Rams in his first season after leaving Detroit. “We had most of the pieces there in Detroit. And so for me, when he won Super Bowl, literally the first year after he left Detroit, I’m out there like, ‘I mean, I told y’all what we had.’” Stafford’s success with the Rams reinforced Johnson’s belief that the Lions had been closer to competing for a title than their lack of championship success suggested. With the NFL trade deadline approaching, Detroit fans are hoping general manager Brad Holmes can strengthen the roster as the team looks to maintain its position in the NFC North. Johnson’s comments also come after years of tension between him and the Lions following his retirement. The organisation once sought $1.6 million back from his signing bonus after he walked away before completing his contract. However, those differences have since faded. Johnson has returned to Ford Field to support the team and has earned places on the Lions’ All-Time Team and Ring of Honor. Now, with Detroit still chasing its first Super Bowl title, his message remains clear: having the talent is not enough if the organisation is unwilling to make the moves needed to finish the job. item.title: Como boss Cesc Fabregas admits he was 'angry' to concede despite breaking Italian away scoring record in 9-1 Champions League win at Lens
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-LENS-COMO - AFP Como head coach Cesc Fabregas expressed frustration over failing to keep a clean sheet even after watching his side dismantle Lens 9-1 on Wednesday night. No Italian club had previously managed seven away goals in European Cup or Champions League history before the Serie A visitors ran riot in France. Italian visitors rewrite history books Fabregas saw his maiden Champions League away win slightly soured by a second-half consolation strike as Como recorded their sixth consecutive victory across all competitions. Having beaten RB Leipzig and Manchester United 4-1 at home either side of a 3-2 loss at Feyenoord, the visitors climbed to fourth in the standings despite missing Moise Kean, Trevoh Chalobah, Assane Diao, Jesus Rodriguez and Jayden Addai. Tournament top scorer Tasos Douvikas netted a treble to score in all four European outings, while Nico Paz, Lucas Da Cunha, Marc-Oliver Kempf, Mattia Liberali, Martin Baturina and 18-year-old debutant Matteo Papaccioli also struck. Manager urges humility after rout Speaking to Sky Sport Italia about sitting fourth midway through the league phase, Fabregas smiled: "It is also our fourth ever Champions League game, so four is the key number here. "I'm happy, this is football and everything went our way. The lads did well, now we have to prepare for a very important match on Sunday, the ninth in a run between breaks for international duty." Urging his young squad to stay grounded after their historic display, the Spaniard added: "It is a wonderful night for Como, for all our fans and many lads here who are at the start of their careers, but they need to keep their feet on the ground, be humble, keep learning and not think everything will go well from here on. "They must keep working to continue these performances." Defensive lapse frustrates former midfielder Despite almost every goal coming from slick passing moves out from the back and an early penalty against Maxence Caqueret being overturned by VAR, Como are still waiting for their first European shutout after conceding a 65th-minute corner volley. Reflecting on that solitary blemish, Fabregas confessed: "I am angry over the goal we conceded, as we changed something in our defending with the three substitutions. "Plus it was scored by a former teammate of mine, I played with Ruben Aguilar at Monaco, and I told him I'd never seen you score a goal like that before! It was honestly a great goal." Defending champions await this weekend Como must now shift their focus back to domestic duties ahead of a challenging Serie A Matchday 11 trip to reigning Scudetto holders Inter on Sunday , November 8, prior to the international break. On the continental front, the Lariani will resume their league phase campaign by hosting AEK Athens and visiting Real Betis. Fabregas' men will then wrap up their schedule against Paris Saint-Germain before travelling to Barcelona on January 27.

What happened next became one of the defining sequences in their 30-18 upset: a run stuffed at the line, a false start, two incompletions and a field goal. Two weeks after a loss at Wisconsin in which several players said teammates hadn't picked each other up properly, the sequence gave the defense the proof it was looking for. "I feel like that was a statement for us as a defense," he said. "Just not giving up a blade of grass. You just never give up." Wafle tied it directly to the trust the group has talked about all season. "You're back on your heels...how are you going to respond, and how are you going to show up for your teammate? Everybody showed up. It's all about trust." The defense earned another gift in the third quarter when linebacker Desman Stephens II punched out a fumble that eventually landed in the arms of defensive tackle Floyd Boucard. What’s interesting is that the Bruins weren’t exactly having a great October as a team. They finished the month 4-6-0-0, scoring 30 goals and allowing 30. The 6-7 point guard, originally hailing from Milwaukee Juneau, Wisconsin, will play his senior high school season with East River in Orlando, Florida. Another high-level backcourt talent from the Class of 2027 is four-star combo guard Jalen Davis, who recently named the Zags as one of his top-four schools, along with the Washington Huskies, UCLA Bruins, and North Carolina Tar Heels. He doesn’t have a commitment date yet. NEWS: 2027 Top-25 overall recruit Jalen Davis is down to four schools, he told @Rivals : ⁰⁰Gonzaga, North Carolina, UCLA, and Washington⁰⁰The 6-foot-3 senior is one of the top guards in the 2027 class. https://t.co/Za8P3EM19D pic.twitter.com/IiprrPopn4 — Joe Tipton (@JoeTipton) November 3, 2026 The 6-3 prospect from Bremerton, Washington, will take an official visit to campus in Spokane, Washington, on Nov. 7 for Gonzaga’s 2026-27 home opener against the Conference USA’s New Mexico State Aggies. Wednesday evening at Ashland Community Stadium, the Bobcats found themselves back in a regional semifinal against Mansfield Christian and made program history in a 5-1 win advancing to their first regional championship. And just before halftime, it was Mansfield Christian who found a breakthrough on a lobbed through ball that skipped on the turf and over the defense where Jacoby Dickinson was able to latch onto it and slot past Norwayne's Garrett Ponting with 41 seconds to go in the half. "We spent too long settling into the game," Mansfield Christian coach Kaedon Anderson said. "When we did, we started playing our style of soccer and had a lot of success. What the Flames couldn't anticipate was the tenacity the Bobcats opened the second half with. A shot from Lysander Bauman deflected off a Mansfield Christian player and out for a corner kick with 32:20 on the clock. Up steps Zollinger who proceeds to score an olimpico directly from the corner in the 49th minute to bring the teams level. item.title: Justin Herbert reacts to opponent saying he’s ‘seeing ghosts’
item.description: Nov 1, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert (10) at press conference after the game against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Chargers are still searching for their first win of the season, and quarterback Justin Herbert has been at the center of their struggles. After Sunday’s 24-9 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, one of the players who intercepted him didn’t hold back. Rams safety Quentin Lake said that Herbert was “seeing ghosts” in the game, adding that he was “throwing deli meat out there.” It was a brutal critique of a quarterback who is supposed to be the face of the franchise. On Wednesday, both Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh and Herbert himself were asked about Lake’s comments. Needless to say, Harbaugh did not see things the same way. Chargers’ Winless Start Sunday’s loss dropped the Chargers to 0-7, making them the only winless team left in the NFL. It’s the franchise’s worst start since 2000. Herbert completed 24 of his 32 passes for 257 yards against the Rams, but he didn’t throw a touchdown and was intercepted twice. Lake picked him off on a short pass early in the game and returned it 45 yards, setting up a Rams field goal, and Trent McDuffie later added a second interception. The Chargers’ offense has been a mess all season. They have scored just 99 points through seven games, and they haven’t found the end zone in their last nine quarters. Herbert, meanwhile, has thrown at least one interception in every game this season. ‘Seeing ghosts’ Lake appeared on the St. Brown Podcast after the game and offered a blunt assessment of Herbert’s performance. “He was throwing deli meat out there,” Lake said, via the St. Brown Podcast . “He’s seeing ghosts. I don’t know what’s going on, but we knew we were gonna get a couple. At least one.” Harbaugh, however, pushed back on that critique when asked about it on Wednesday. “As far as anybody’s opinion I don’t see that,” Harbaugh told reporters . “Everybody’s entitled to their opinion. Not what I see.” He actually thought Herbert played well against the Rams. “I thought he played — did his job exceptionally well,” Harbaugh said. “You know, two throws he would have liked to have back.” Herbert, for his part, claimed that he hadn’t even heard about Lake’s comments. “I haven’t looked into it, haven’t heard anything about it, so I can’t really make a comment about it,” Herbert told reporters . “We’re really just focused on what’s going on in the building, playing football and doing what we can and doing our best to, you know, go put our best effort out on Sunday. item.title: Player grades: SGA's 42 points lead Thunder to 124-116 win over Cavaliers
item.description: OKLAHOMA CITY — Dribbling the ball between his legs, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander stared down his next victim. As Tyrese Proctor was left alone on an island, the two-time MVP vindicated his outside-happy shot diet. He drilled a stepback 3-pointer that sealed another momentum-building night in their new NBA reality. The Oklahoma City Thunder came out with ample energy in a 124-116 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers . They're slowly relearning how to play without Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace. Super-sizing the starting lineup, the Thunder absolutely ran the Cavaliers out of the gym from the jump. Kenrich Williams knocked down an outside jumper. He slashed to the rim. The ball ping-ponged around as Alex Caruso's return from a three-game absence was met with roaring applause. It didn't take long for the Thunder to put up some wacky scores. At one point, it was 25-9. And then 30-15. They had a 37-20 lead after the first quarter. Pretty surreal to see them completely out-energize Donovan Mitchell and James Harden. The onslaught continued in the second frame. At one point, the Thunder doubled up the Cavaliers on the scoreboard, 50-25. The second unit kept the momentum going as the Cavaliers looked half-asleep and ready to get out of town in their sole trip to OKC of the year. The Thunder had 23 points in the second frame. They entered halftime with a 60-44 lead over the Cavaliers. Coming out of the halftime break, the Cavaliers tried to make up ground quickly. They rattled off the first nine points of the second half. Harden drained an outside jumper through contact. And then Mitchell went coast-to-coast for a fastbreak layup. Once OKC saw its lead fall to single-digit points, Gilgeous-Alexander quit with the trolling shot diet of pull-up 3-pointers. He returned to his bread and butter. Overall, the Thunder rebounded well. They had 28 points in the third quarter. That kept them a healthy distance from the Cavaliers with an 88-74 lead. For the most part, OKC stiff-armed Cleveland on the scoreboard. Micah Peavy has provided a jolt of defensive energy. So did Caruso — per usual. After Caruso fed Aday Mara a dump-off pass for a cutting dunk, that felt like the punctuation mark. The Thunder had a 111-93 lead with a little under four minutes to go. Of course, the Cavaliers made a fake hot run. Mitchell tried his best Tracy McGrady impersonation by knocking down unconscious deep jumpers. Alas, all that did was extent the game by about a dozen minutes. Also helped Gilgeous-Alexander cross 40 points for a second consecutive game. The Thunder had 36 points in the fourth quarter. That was just enough to keep up with Cleveland's high-scoring 42 points in the final frame. Needing a morale boost. OKC's two-game sweep over the Cavaliers has brought most of the fanbase back into the cautiously optimistic side of things. The Thunder shot 46% from the field and went 15-of-36 (41.7%) from 3. They shot 27-of-35 on free throws. They had 25 assists on 41 baskets.
